changed this: What changed

Composer ported from web (components/Composer.tsx) — bordered card holding a + actions menu, the input, and a single send-or-stop control that never shows both, with the web's teaching reminder underneath ("keating won't give you the answer — that's the point"). The menu carries Live, Model, and Thinking. The web's right-hand "enter to send" hint is omitted because web hides it on mobile too.

Light mode — theme preference (System/Light/Dark) in a new UiSettingsProvider layered above the theme provider so the stored choice is known before first paint. This surfaced a real bug: the accent green is only contrast-validated as a background, but was used as text colour throughout — 3.04:1 on the light surface. Added a primaryText role (accentText, 4.96:1) and moved every text/icon usage onto it; dark mode is pixel-identical since the two roles coincide there. Splash now has a light default with a dark variant.

Settings — Appearance (theme, font), Chat (interactive cards, raw provider errors, thinking budget), About You. Each is wired to real behaviour rather than stored and ignored:
- Font installs JetBrains Mono + Roboto and flows typography through the theme (theme.type), so the setting restyles the whole app.
- Thinking budget maps per provider (OpenAI reasoning.effort, Anthropic thinking.budget_tokens with max_tokens raised above it and temperature yielded, Gemini thinkingConfig) and is only sent for models the catalog says support it. While adding this I found Gemini's thought parts would have leaked into replies — now filtered in both the streaming and non-streaming parsers.
- Raw errors keeps the provider's text and derives a friendly summary when off, so the toggle works retroactively on an error already on screen.
- About You appends to the system prompt as JSON-fenced background, mirroring the web's framing so it can't override the teaching protocol.

Live — off the tab bar, entered from the composer. Note the Live screen itself is unchanged: it still explains native Live isn't in this build and links to web. I only moved the entry point, as asked.

Courses — native client: /session, list, join-by-code, and course detail with modules, expandable lessons, materials, and members. Teacher access is an explicit opt-in switch on the join sheet, never implied by joining. "Study this with Keating" handch exposed a latent bug wherenewSession() followed by sendMessage() in one tick posted into the previous session; the state ref now        updates synchronously.
                                                                                                              Two things worth flagging: the web settoxy, share links, animation renderer,flashcards, artifact toggles) per your scope choice, and course authoring/discussion/review remain web-only — the detail screen says so and links outwise. Cookie handling uses an explicitjar rather than trusting RN's native persistence; I haven't run it against a live server, so that's the piece I'd verify first on device.
 Continue from there

Status: **in progress**

The mobile tranche is implemented, documented, and source-matched to an installed Android release.

- [Build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:75) now defines exact-model controls, typography parity, authenticated Courses behavior, consent, materials, and atomic Tutor handoff.
- [Execution plan and pseudocode](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430) records the checkpoint and prevents incomplete M3/M4 work from being counted.

Accepted:

- P0 and D1.
- Internal foundations D2a and M1a remain accepted but contribute no independent progress.

Verified:

- Mobile: 110 tests passing, 420 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript check passed.
- Android export: 2,005 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB Hermes bundle.
- Release APK: 100.1 MB, 946 Gradle tasks.
- Final post-fix APK installed and running on the connected Pixel.
- Local authenticated Courses flow passed through protected 19,778-byte material retrieval.
- Installed app correctly surfaces deployed Courses authentication failure and recovery.

Waiting:

- C1/C2 require the requested Luna review. Luna is unavailable in the current agent/model inventory and no local Luna executable exists. Terra-high review was used.
- Deployed Courses returns `503 notorganic_auth_adapter_unavailable`.
- Picture-in-picture obscures current device captures, so they do not establish look parity.

Completion blockers include native attachments and grounding recovery, complete settings, hosted wallet/token checkout, decks/SRS/profile, native Live, full course collaboration/offline conflicts, public sharing, iOS acceptance, desktop/TUI completion, and clean physical visual comparisons.

`vet` was invoked after each logical change but produced no verdict because it cannot reconstruct the large existing dirty-worktree diff (`DiffApplicationError`).

The mobile gap is now partially closed.

- Added a native [Usage & Study Activity page](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/usage.tsx:20), reachable from [More](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/(tabs)/more.tsx:21).
- It reports real local lessons, messages, attachments, artifacts, feedback, study topics, models, provider-reported tokens, and reported cost.
- It explicitly does not fabricate mastery. Quiz evidence, goals, SRS, retention, learner confidence, historical usage, and portable cross-platform records still require the shared learner repository.
- New replies now persist normalized provider/model/token usage. Older replies cannot retroactively recover missing token data.

The composer now supports images and documents through [Add images / Add documents](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/Composer.tsx:154), including validation, draft recovery, removal, transcript rendering, and provider-specific OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and OpenRouter payloads. The Impeccable pass kept these controls compact and recoverable.

Verification:

- 123 mobile tests pass, 448 assertions.
- Strict TypeScript passes.
- Android export: 2,010 modules, 36 assets, 5.5 MB bundle.
- Release build: 946 Gradle tasks.
- Updated APK installed and launched on the connected Pixel.
- On-device verification confirmed the Usage page and attachment menu.
- I did not select a personal device file, so pick → preview → send remains unaccepted.
- Vet remains unverified because it crashes reconstructing the existing dirty worktree.

On self-augmentation:

- Mobile: no. It cannot rewrite its installed application or this repository.
- Normal web: can modify only its sandbox workspace.
- Locally hosted web with a project root and `--allow-local-exec`: can modify the actual checkout.
- TUI/Pi: yes. Its `edit`, `write`, and `bash` tools can change the working directory.
- `auto-improve`: changes policy and evolved-prompt artifacts; it does not automatically rewrite source code.

The host web and TUI mutation paths should gain an explicit preview/diff/confirmation/validation gate before being considered safe product behavior.

I updated the [build specification](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:118), [baseline](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-baseline.md:54), and [execution checkpoint](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:430). `/goal` remains active at 11.7% evidence-weighted completion: these additions do not yet satisfy the full M3 learner-data, Live, recovery, iOS, visual-parity, or required Luna-review gates.
